dau-phu-dap-hanh-chay-ha-noi.name: Hanoi-Style Vegetarian Tofu Dipped in Scallion Sauce
aliases: Fried tofu dipped in scallion soy sauce
dau-phu-dap-hanh-chay-ha-noi.serving_basis: Four portions of tofu served with rice or porridge as a side for a vegetarian family meal.
dau-phu-dap-hanh-chay-ha-noi.description: A Bếp Việt plant-based version inspired by the old Hanoi technique of quickly dipping hot tofu into a seasoned scallion bowl. Golden fried tofu is dipped briefly in diluted soy sauce and scallions so it absorbs flavor while staying soft.
dau-phu-dap-hanh-chay-ha-noi.finished_dish: The tofu is lightly golden with a soft center, coated in green scallions and gently savory-sweet; the soy sauce forms a light coating rather than soaking in.
dau-phu-dap-hanh-chay-ha-noi.serving: Serve hot with plain rice or mung bean porridge. Dip each piece as soon as it is fried so the scallions just wilt and the tofu stays hot.
tips: Pat the tofu dry before frying to reduce splatter; fry in batches so the oil temperature does not drop.
Use a fully plant-based soy sauce; this version replaces the fish sauce and pork fat in the source description.
Dip both sides quickly, since soaking makes the tofu too salty and soft.
dish_type: Fried tofu dipped in scallion sauce
search_terms: tofu dipped in scallion soy sauce
dau-phu-dap-hanh-chay-ha-noi.image_alt: Golden fried tofu quickly dipped in soy sauce and scallions, served on a white ceramic plate.
dau-phu-dap-hanh-chay-ha-noi.time_note: About 40 minutes, including 10 minutes to press the tofu; dip quickly while hot.

ingredients.name: Firm white tofu
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh tofu, drain and gently press before cutting.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse, dry and finely slice both the green and white parts.

ingredients.name: Vegan soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a type with no fish or seafood ingredients.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Dilutes the soy sauce so the tofu is only lightly seasoned.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Reduce or omit if the soy sauce is already mild.

ingredients.name: Neutral vegetable oil
ingredients.notes: Use enough for shallow frying; the tofu absorbs less than the amount added to the pan.

preparation_steps.instruction: Place the tofu on a rack, cover with a clean towel and press gently for about 10 minutes to drain. Cut into 3–4 cm squares.
Rinse and dry the scallions, then finely slice them. Stir the soy sauce, water and sugar together in a shallow bowl and mix in the scallions.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil over medium heat. Fry the tofu in batches for about 3–4 minutes per side until lightly golden and hot throughout; drain on a rack.
While the tofu is still hot, dip each piece quickly into the scallion soy mixture, turn both sides and transfer to a plate; do not leave the tofu soaking.
Spoon any remaining scallions over the tofu and serve immediately with rice or porridge.

ca-bung-chay-bac-bo.name: Northern Vietnamese Vegetarian Eggplant Stew
aliases: Plant-based Northern-style eggplant and tofu stew
ca-bung-chay-bac-bo.serving_basis: Four portions of eggplant stewed with tofu, served with plain rice or rice vermicelli.
ca-bung-chay-bac-bo.description: A Bếp Việt plant-based version inspired by Northern eggplant stew: eggplant simmers with tomato, fermented rice, turmeric and herbs, with fried tofu for a nutty bite. It omits meat and shrimp paste and uses vegan soy sauce to keep the dish fully plant-based.
ca-bung-chay-bac-bo.finished_dish: The eggplant is tender but intact, the tofu is seasoned, and the pale golden broth is lightly thick with gentle sourness from fermented rice; perilla and lolot are aromatic.
ca-bung-chay-bac-bo.serving: Ladle into a bowl or small clay pot while hot. Finish with scallions, perilla and lolot, and serve with plain rice or rice vermicelli.
tips: Soak the eggplant in salted water with a little vinegar, then rinse and drain to reduce browning; stew until fully tender.
Use mature, pleasantly sour fermented rice and strain it; add seasoning gradually because acidity and saltiness vary.
Stir gently after adding eggplant so the pieces keep their shape; add the herbs at the end to preserve their aroma.
search_terms: vegetarian eggplant stew with fermented rice
Northern Vietnamese eggplant and tofu stew
ca-bung-chay-bac-bo.image_alt: A bowl of vegetarian eggplant stew with eggplant, tofu, tomato, perilla and lolot in golden broth.
ca-bung-chay-bac-bo.time_note: About 65 minutes, including a 20-minute eggplant soak; simmer gently until tender but not broken down.

ingredients.name: Eggplant
ingredients.notes: Choose firm, glossy fruit and cut into bite-size wedges.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Cut into 2 cm cubes, pat dry and lightly fry until golden.

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.notes: Cut into wedges.

ingredients.name: Mature fermented rice starter
ingredients.notes: Strain through a sieve; use pleasantly sour fermented rice with no signs of spoilage.

ingredients.name: Fresh turmeric
ingredients.notes: Grate or finely chop; ground turmeric may also be used.

ingredients.name: Dried shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add enough to stew the eggplant; it need not be fully submerged.

ingredients.name: Vegan soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a type with no fish or seafood ingredients.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use 8 g for the eggplant soak and rinse it off; season the stew with the remaining 3 g.

ingredients.name: Rice vinegar
ingredients.notes: Add to the soaking water to reduce browning; do not pour it into the stew.

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.notes: Used to lightly fry the tofu and saute the aromatics.

ingredients.name: Perilla
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice into thin strips.

ingredients.name: Lolot leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice into thin strips.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and finely slice.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse the eggplant and cut into wedges about 3 cm thick. Soak for 20 minutes in 1 litre of water with 8 g salt and the vinegar. Rinse and drain.
Pat the tofu dry and cut into cubes; cut the tomato into wedges. Chop the shallots, garlic and turmeric; strain the fermented rice and slice the perilla, lolot and scallions.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat half the oil and lightly fry the tofu until golden on all sides; remove. Add the remaining oil, saute the shallots and garlic, then stir in the turmeric and tomato for 2–3 minutes.
Add the eggplant and stir gently. Add the water, fermented rice, soy sauce and 3 g salt; cover and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes until the eggplant is tender.
Add the tofu and simmer for 3 more minutes. Taste, turn off the heat and fold in the perilla, lolot and scallions. Serve hot.

canh-muop-nau-lac-tay-bac.name: Northwest Vietnamese Luffa and Peanut Soup
canh-muop-nau-lac-tay-bac.serving_basis: One pot of luffa and fresh peanut soup for four people to eat with rice.
canh-muop-nau-lac-tay-bac.description: Luffa and peanut soup is a simple family dish recalled from a Northwest Vietnamese home kitchen. Crushed fresh peanuts are cooked first until soft and nutty, then luffa is added to keep its light sweetness. This Bếp Việt version uses plant-based oil and seasonings.
canh-muop-nau-lac-tay-bac.finished_dish: The broth is light and clear, the peanuts are soft with a little texture, and the green luffa is tender but not mushy; scallions and Vietnamese coriander smell fresh.
canh-muop-nau-lac-tay-bac.serving: Ladle into a soup bowl and finish with scallions, Vietnamese coriander and a little pepper. Serve hot with plain rice; it is best just after cooking.
tips: Crush the peanuts moderately so they release their nutty flavor without making the broth too thick.
Cook the peanuts until tender before adding the luffa; the gourd cooks quickly, so simmer it only for the final few minutes.
Peanuts are a common allergen; tell guests clearly that the soup contains them.
canh-muop-nau-lac-tay-bac.image_alt: A bowl of green luffa soup with crushed peanuts and scallions in a light ceramic bowl.
canh-muop-nau-lac-tay-bac.time_note: About 40 minutes; cook the peanuts until tender before adding the luffa for the last few minutes.

ingredients.name: Luffa gourd
ingredients.notes: Choose young, firm fruit; peel thinly and slice about 1 cm thick.

ingredients.name: Shelled fresh peanuts
ingredients.notes: Rinse and crush coarsely; if using dry raw peanuts, soak for 2 hours first.

ingredients.name: Dried shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and thinly slice.

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.notes: Used to saute the shallots instead of pork fat.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Reduce slightly if you prefer a thicker soup.

ingredients.name: Vegan soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a type with no fish or seafood ingredients; it replaces fish sauce in this vegetarian version.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season gradually after the peanuts and luffa release their flavor.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Sawtooth coriander
ingredients.notes: Rinse and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Add to taste at the end.

preparation_steps.instruction: Peel the luffa, remove any tough fibers, rinse and cut into slices about 1 cm thick. Rinse and coarsely crush the peanuts.
Peel and slice the shallots. Rinse the scallions and Vietnamese coriander, then finely slice them; keep them aside for the end.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil in a pot and saute the shallots until fragrant. Add the peanuts and stir for 1–2 minutes. Add the water, bring to a boil, then simmer for 12–18 minutes until the peanuts are tender, skimming foam if needed.
Add the luffa and simmer for 3–5 minutes until just tender. Season with soy sauce and salt, taste and turn off the heat.
Add the scallions, Vietnamese coriander and pepper. Ladle into a bowl and serve hot.

dua-cai-cu-muoi-xoi-bac-bo.name: Northern Vietnamese Quick-Pickled Mustard Greens and Radish
dua-cai-cu-muoi-xoi-bac-bo.serving_basis: One small jar of quick-pickled mustard greens and radish as a side for four people over several meals.
dua-cai-cu-muoi-xoi-bac-bo.description: A cool-season Northern Vietnamese side dish of mustard leaves, stalks and radish lightly fermented in a mild salt-and-sugar brine until crisp, yellow-green and gently sour. This small-batch version is ready after about one day of mild fermentation.
dua-cai-cu-muoi-xoi-bac-bo.finished_dish: The stalks are crisp, the leaves are yellow-green and the radish slices are translucent; the flavor is mildly salty and tart, without slime or off odors.
dua-cai-cu-muoi-xoi-bac-bo.serving: Use clean chopsticks to take a small portion, drain it and serve with rice, tofu or a braised dish. Rinse briefly if it tastes too salty.
tips: Use a clean glass or ceramic jar that has been scalded and dried; keep all vegetables fully submerged beneath the brine.
Check the flavor after 24 hours because warmer rooms ferment faster; refrigerate once it reaches the desired mild sourness.
Discard the whole jar if mold, stringy slime, a rotten smell or an unusual color appears; do not taste food that shows spoilage.
search_terms: Northern Vietnamese quick pickled mustard greens and radish
dua-cai-cu-muoi-xoi-bac-bo.image_alt: A bowl of yellow-green quick-pickled mustard greens and radish with crisp stalks and a few red chili rings.
dua-cai-cu-muoi-xoi-bac-bo.time_note: About 24 hours 30 minutes, including one day of mild fermentation; it may sour sooner in a warm room.

ingredients.name: Fresh mustard greens with radish
ingredients.notes: Choose firm stalks and undamaged leaves; rinse thoroughly and drain the surface water.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Boil, then cool until warm before pouring over the greens.

ingredients.name: Coarse salt
ingredients.notes: Dissolve completely in the water; about 2.7% of the water weight.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Softens the brine; reduce slightly if preferred.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash thoroughly and use both the white roots and green stems.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Rinse and remove seeds for less heat; may be omitted.

preparation_steps.instruction: Discard bruised leaves and rinse the greens several times under clean running water. Split thick stalks lengthwise and cut into serving lengths; peel and slice any radish roots.
Wash the scallions and chili. Wash the jar, lid and a clean weight with hot water, then let them dry completely. Boil the water, dissolve the salt and sugar, and cool below 35°C.

cooking_steps.instruction: Pack the greens, radish, scallions and chili into the jar. Pour in enough cooled brine to cover them, weigh them down with a clean weight and close the lid.
Leave in a cool, airy place for about 24 hours, then taste using a clean utensil. Once mildly sour and yellow-green, refrigerate; keep the remaining vegetables submerged.

cu-nieng-xao-trung-bac-bo.name: Northern Delta Stir-Fried Water Bamboo Shoots with Egg
aliases: Northern Vietnamese Water Bamboo Shoots with Egg
Stir-Fried Water bamboo shoots with Egg
cu-nieng-xao-trung-bac-bo.serving_basis: One plate of seasonal water bamboo shoots and egg for four people with rice.
cu-nieng-xao-trung-bac-bo.description: Thin slices of water bamboo shoots are quickly stir-fried with egg, shallot and herbs. This is a seasonal vegetable dish of the Northern Delta; the Bếp Việt version uses vegetable oil and salt instead of pork fat and fish sauce used in some preparations.
cu-nieng-xao-trung-bac-bo.finished_dish: The shoots are just tender and still crisp, the egg is softly set around them, and scallions and cilantro are fragrant; the plate is not watery.
cu-nieng-xao-trung-bac-bo.serving: Serve hot with freshly cooked rice and finish with pepper. Avoid covering the plate for long so the shoots keep their crispness.
tips: Choose firm shoots with fresh sheaths; slice evenly and stir-fry over medium-high heat for a short time.
Add the egg when the shoots are just tender and stir until the egg is fully cooked.
This version uses oil and salt and contains egg; it is not vegan.
search_terms: Northern Delta stir fried water bamboo shoots with egg
cu-nieng-xao-trung-bac-bo.image_alt: A plate of thinly sliced water bamboo shoots stir-fried with set egg, scallions and cilantro.
cu-nieng-xao-trung-bac-bo.time_note: About 25 minutes; stir-fry briefly and cook the egg fully.

ingredients.name: Fresh water bamboo shoots
ingredients.notes: Peel away tough sheaths, rinse, trim the hard base and slice diagonally thin.

ingredients.name: Chicken eggs
ingredients.notes: Crack into a clean bowl, beat with a pinch of salt.

ingredients.name: Dried shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and thinly slice.

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.notes: Replaces pork fat in this edited version.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use some to season the beaten eggs and the rest for the shoots.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into short lengths.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into short lengths.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle on after turning off the heat.

preparation_steps.instruction: Peel away the old brown sheaths of the shoots, rinse, trim hard ends and cut into even diagonal slices about 2–3 mm thick.
Peel and slice the shallots. Crack the eggs into a clean bowl, add a pinch of salt and beat; rinse and cut the scallions and cilantro.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil in a pan and saute the shallots until fragrant. Add the shoots and stir-fry over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes until just tender but still crisp; season with the remaining salt.
Spread the shoots evenly, pour in the egg and gently stir until the egg is fully cooked and set around the slices. Add the scallions, cilantro and pepper, then turn off the heat.
